chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Sa'dan, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He (peace be upon him) used to say in his prostration: 'My worn-out face prostrates to Your Remaining, Everlasting, Magnificent Face. My humble face prostrates to Your Honorable Face. My poor face prostrates to the Face of my Lord, the Self-Sufficient, the Generous, the Exalted, the Magnificent.'

O Lord, I seek Your forgiveness from what has been and I seek Your forgiveness from what will be. O Lord, do not exhaust my afflictions. O Lord, do not let my enemies gloat over me. O Lord, do not make my decree bad.

O Lord, indeed there is no Defender nor Preventer except You. Send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad with the best of Your blessings, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad with the best of Your blessings.
O Allah, I seek refuge in You from Your seizures, and I seek refuge in You from all Your anger and wrath. Glory be to You, there is no god except You, Lord of the worlds.

And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say while prostrating: 'Have mercy on my humility before You, and my supplication to You, and my loneliness from the people, and make me comfortable with You, O Generous One.'

And he used to say also: 'You advised me but I did not heed, and You deterred me from Your prohibitions but I did not desist, and You enriched me with Your favors but I did not thank You for Your pardon. Your pardon, O Generous One! I ask You for ease at death, and I ask You for pardon at the reckoning.'

And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say while prostrating: 'There is no god except You, truly, truly! I prostrated to You, O Lord, in submission and servitude. O Magnificent, indeed my deed is weak, so multiply it for me. O Generous, O Gracious, forgive my sins and my crime, and accept my deed. O Generous, O Compeller, I seek refuge in You from failing or bearing injustice.'
O Allah, from You is the bounty, and You provide its gratitude, and upon You is the reward of what You bestowed from its reward, by the grace of Your prolongation and the nobility of its return.

key_terms.الرَّاحَةَ عِنْدَ الْمَوْتِ: Ease/Relief at the time of death

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications to recite during prostration according to Shia Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the profound theological depth of the prostration posture, where the Imams articulate the dialectic between human fragility and Divine permanence through specific epithets like 'the Perishing' and 'the Eternal'. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *tawadu'* (humility) and *istighfar* (seeking forgiveness), linking physical submission with spiritual reliance on God’s mercy to counteract the fear of enemies and the weight of sins. The inclusion of distinct supplications from the Prophet’s family serves as a normative model for integrating gratitude, self-reflection, and divine attributes into daily worship.
